descriptionChirho: Masculine noun denoting a small wild canid, encompassing both foxes and jackals, as Biblical Hebrew does not consistently distinguish between the two animals. English translations vary between 'foxes' and 'jackals' depending on context (Lam 5:18 favors 'jackals,' Judg 15:4 and Song 2:15 favor 'foxes'), but the Hebrew lexeme covers both referents as a single semantic category. All four clusters show the same noun with grammatical variation: plural, singular, with preposition כ (like). Arabic ثَعَالِب/ثَعْلَب (foxes/fox) is used across all clusters without distinction. Korean 여우 (fox), Spanish zorras/zorros (foxes), Hindi लोमड़ी/सियार/गीदड़ (fox/jackal), and Swahili mbweha (fox/jackal) confirm the unified sense.
